method.sample: GitHub search API: q=created:>2026-10-21, sort=stars, order=desc, per_page=40
method.readme_scan: 40 READMEs fetched via /repos/{r}/readme, decoded from base64, matched against naive and word-boundary regexes
method.events_scan: /repos/{r}/events (rolling window, up to 3x100 events) -> WatchEvent timestamps bucketed at 1min and 5min

readme_scan.false_positive_cause: pattern 'irm\s+' matches the tail of the word 'confirm'

baseline_for_comparison.2026-10-05: 4 of the top 10 newly created repos were single-file README farms with 0 forks, 0 releases, no license
baseline_for_comparison.2026-10-14: one repo showed 22+20+4 stars inside three consecutive minutes (WatchEvent clustering)
baseline_for_comparison.2026-10-29: 0 of 40 have forks==0; densest 5-minute bucket is 7.6% of a repo's sampled stars

caveats: Forks and stars are snapshots, not time series; a farm can add fake forks too.
/events exposes only the last ~300 events, so arrival shape is a rolling window.
Stars can also be bought slowly (a few per hour) with real accounts; shape probes miss that.
Absence of a signature is not proof of legitimacy.
